title: Intelligent canary orchestration with semantics-aware routing and cost-tier fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current rollout primitives at Redwood provide traffic splitting and basic fallbacks but lack an end-to-end orchestration that reasons about: (1) semantic compatibility between model variants (not just model size), (2) regional capacity signals and cost tiers, and (3) automated rollback that factors in both quality regressions and cross-region availability. Goal: Build an intelligent canary orchestration layer that performs progressive ramps, shadow checks, and automated tier-aware fallback routing with clear observable triggers for rollback.

Scope and constraints:
- Only affects runtime routing and rollout controller (no model training changes).
- Must integrate with existing Console rollout UI and tracing hooks.
- Must be compatible with Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Maintain existing latency SLOs where possible; if not, document trade-offs.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Semantic compatibility checks: before sending production traffic to a canary variant, run a short set of production prompt fingerprints and structured-output validators against canary outputs in shadow mode. Compute a lightweight semantic-drift score (embedding distance + token-level schema checks). Gate traffic ramp if score exceeds threshold.
2) Cost-tier fallback routing: classify serving nodes into tiers (premium/dedicated, standard, low-cost-quantized). If primary tier signals capacity pressure or cost budget triggers, dynamically route new requests to compatible lower-cost variants subject to compatibility checks. Maintain sticky routing for sessions where stateful KV cache compatibility cannot be guaranteed.
3) Region-aware failover: monitor per-region capacity and latency inflation. On region degradation (latency > SLO or error rate spike), automatically failover only stateless requests to next eligible region; stateful requests follow a conservative path (try warm-cache regional replica or funnel to matte-mode responses).
4) Progressive canary behavior: start with 0% traffic -> shadow-only validation window -> 1% production traffic -> geometric ramp (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%) with hold windows and automated quality checks after each step. Allow manual override from Console.
5) Auto-rollback: triggers include sustained semantic drift above threshold, generation-level regression alerts from evals tied to prompt sets, error-rate and latency SLO breaches, and third-party customer error spikes. Rollback should perform a soft-fail where traffic re-routes to the last-known-good variant and a postmortem is automatically opened if rollback occurred.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can perform a full canary progression with semantic checks and can be exercised in staging with synthetic load.
- Console shows step-level metrics (semantic-drift, latency, error-rate, token-cost) and allows abort/resume.
- Automatic rollback initiates within 60s of a triggering condition and the end-to-end switch completes within defined SLA for the release.
- Region failover can be simulated in chaos testing and respects stateful routing guards.

Metrics to track:
- Semantic-drift score distribution per canary run
- Time-to-detect and time-to-rollback for regressions
- Cost delta when falling back to lower tiers
- Percentage of sessions requiring sticky routing vs stateless routes

Implementation tasks (engineering checklist):
- [ ] Implement shadow validator that computes embedding-based drift and schema checks (ENG-34108 planned subtask).
- [ ] Extend routing policy engine to support tiered target lists and weight adjustments based on capacity signals (ENG-34109).
- [ ] Add region-capacity-monitoring hooks and failover state machine (ENG-34110).
- [ ] Console UX changes: step visualization and manual controls (coord with PM/Design).
- [ ] Integrate with existing rollback automation and incident creation APIs.
- [ ] Add canary e2e tests and chaos scenarios to CI.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Semantic validations add latency to shadow validation; to mitigate we run them in parallel and keep only a small sample set for gating.
- Routing to low-cost quantized variants can change output characteristics; require stricter compatibility thresholds.
- Private deployments may impose networking constraints; provide a reduced-feature mode that disables cross-region failover for air-gapped customers.

Next steps:
- Sync with PM (Olivia Grant) and Design (Rui Fernandez) this week for Console wireframes and threshold defaults.
- Build prototype shadow validator to run on one active canary in staging.
- Schedule a chaos test for region failover in Cycle 2026-W12.
